newsitem.title: INDIA: Bayer AG to buy Indian polymer firm.
newsitem.headline: Bayer AG to buy Indian polymer firm.

text.p: German chemicals and pharmaceuticals giant Bayer AG plans to acquire Indian polymer maker ABS Industries Ltd, the Indian firm said in a notice to the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday.

Bayer Industries Ltd, a fully-owned subsidiary of Bayer AG, has agreed to acquire up to 5.58 million equity shares, which represents 30.99 percent of the capital, on a preferential basis from ABS Industries, it said.
"The intention of the acquirer is to reach an eventual shareholding of 51 percent," the public notice said.
ABS Industries will issue 6.0 million 10-rupee face value stock at 70 rupees a share on preferential basis, of which 0.42 million shares will be taken up by the current promoters.
Bayer Industries will subsequently make a public offer to buy another 20 percent stake at 70 rupees a share.

"Bayer Industries Ltd together with any other company or companies ....would shortly make an offer to all shareholders of ABS Industries to acquire additional equity shares representing 20 percent of eventual voting capital," the notice said.
The offer has been made to shareholders whose names appear in the books on November 27, and will be open from December 6 to January 3, 1997, it said.
Bayer Industries is a new firm. Bayer AG's holds a 51 percent stake in Bayer India Ltd, a big player in Indian agrochemicals market. It also makes pharmaceuticals.
ABS Industries is a major producer of acrylonitrile butadine styrene (ABS), a polymer or plastic raw material used in automobiles and refrigerators.
The firm reported sales of 1.15 billion rupees in the year to June 30, 1995 and net profit of 165.7 million rupees.
